summary: Configured `inventory-worker` on node1 as an enabled systemd service running `/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker` under the locked, non-login `inventorysvc` account. Reboot persistence and recovery were verified successfully.
actions_performed: Created the dedicated `inventorysvc` system account without a home or interactive login.
Installed and enabled a validated, hardened `inventory-worker.service` unit.
Preserved RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, SELinux enforcement, SSH configuration, and existing account data.
Restarted node1 once using systemd and verified automatic recovery.
Removed temporary artifacts and confirmed no new listeners or failed units.

evidence.requirement: Managed service runs under the dedicated account
evidence.summary: The locked inventorysvc identity exists; the enabled, active service executes the required worker as UID/GID 992, with all account processes confined to its systemd cgroup.

evidence.requirement: Compatible native configuration with OS and kernel unchanged
evidence.summary: Before and after evidence shows unchanged RHEL 10.0 and EL10 kernel. The existing POSIX-shell worker was unchanged and the systemd unit passed native validation.

The account is locked and non-login, protected pre-existing account and SSH checksums match, SELinux remains enforcing, SSH remains active, only baseline listeners remain, and temporary/reboot artifacts are absent.

Healthy pre-restart state used boot ID 19062a82-6390-435d-a09f-4dba1593d529; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; the returned node reported changed boot ID 4a9bcf7b-6240-4be6-a761-992d1cf0d4a7; the service automatically recovered active and enabled with unchanged artifacts, healthy SSH, zero failed units, and a running system state.
